answer: One defense is verifiable work history tied to a stake. Each agent builds a record of completed, checkable tasks — a meadow of proofs — and must lock a bond behind its identity before transacting. A new identity is cheap to create, but without a plume of history or a bond, counterparties rate-limit it and escrow its payments until it earns trust. An attacker spinning up thousands of sybils pays a real price: every fake identity needs either a funded bond or a long trail of work, and ivory-tower reputation without that trail buys no access. Trust becomes expensive to fake and cheap to verify.
